findings.evidence: `harmonicAt_ballGreenCorrector` (Ball.lean:179) already takes exactly `h : 0 < ‖x‖ ^ 2 * ‖y‖ ^ 2 - 2 * ⟪x, y⟫_ℝ + 1`; the new lemma's whole proof body only derives that hypothesis from `hx` and `hy`. `HarmonicOnNhd.mono` exists: mathlib/Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/Harmonic/Basic.lean:101 `lemma HarmonicOnNhd.mono (h : HarmonicOnNhd f s) (hst : t ⊆ s) : HarmonicOnNhd f t`.
findings.fix: State `theorem harmonicOnNhd_ballGreenCorrector {x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)} : HarmonicOnNhd (ballGreenCorrector n x) {y | 0 < ‖x‖ ^ 2 * ‖y‖ ^ 2 - 2 * ⟪x, y⟫_ℝ + 1} := fun y hy => harmonicAt_ballGreenCorrector hy` (plain `Set`, not an `Opens` coercion), and at the use site in DistributionalLaplacian.lean:50,79 specialize with `HarmonicOnNhd.mono` plus `norm_sq_mul_norm_sq_sub_two_mul_inner_add_one_pos`.
findings.issue: `harmonicOnNhd_ballGreenCorrector` restricts the domain to `↑(⟨ball 0 1, isOpen_ball⟩ : Opens _)` and needs `hx : ‖x‖ ≤ 1` only because of that restriction; harmonicity in fact holds, with no hypothesis on `x`, on the whole positivity set of the reflection polynomial. In particular the ball-only form cannot give harmonicity on a neighbourhood of the closed ball for `‖x‖ < 1`, which Ball.lean's module docstring advertises (lines 21, 176-178) and which the Green representation formula needs.

summary: The new corrector-harmonicity lemma is stated at a narrower level than the pointwise lemma it wraps, taking a hypothesis on the pole and a hard-coded unit-ball domain where the hypothesis-free general form is a one-liner. The new test-function Laplacian bridge also re-proves a computation already carried out inline in the same file.
